source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Apply the patch to clean, dry, intact skin and rotate sites with replacement","B":"Expose the patch to heating pads, hot tubs, or saunas while it is in place","C":"Inspect the application site and use a different intact skin area next time","D":"Fold used patches adhesive-side together and follow safe disposal instructions"}}
source_row.rationale: FDA labeling warns that exposing a transdermal fentanyl patch to external heat sources (heating pads, hot tubs, electric blankets, saunas, heated water beds, prolonged direct sunlight, or fever) can significantly increase the rate of fentanyl absorption, leading to potentially fatal overdose. Clients must be taught to avoid heat exposure to the patch area.
source_row.source_detail: Warnings: external heat can increase fentanyl absorption and has resulted in fatal overdose; current label, accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.stem: A client using a transdermal fentanyl patch for chronic pain should be taught to avoid which of the following?
